title: A ruler on a world map
hook: Maps come with a scale bar. Slide one north on a world map and measure again.

doesNotKnow: that on a world map a scale bar is true only along one line

misconception: A map's scale bar measures distance the same way everywhere.
objective: The learner can explain that on a Mercator map the same on-screen length covers less ground farther from the equator (half at 60°), so a single scale bar is true only along one line.

claims.text: On this Mercator map the yellow bar spans 2,000 km at the equator.
claims.source: Demo.tsx sets the bar's screen length to projection.scale() x 2,000 / 6,371.0088 and measures ground distance by inverting both ends: R cos(lat) x difference in longitude, which is 2,000 km at the equator. Design change from the brief: the brief used a 1,000 km bar, which would be under 25 px wide on a phone-width world map; the ratio and the answer ('half') are unchanged.

claims.text: At 60°N the same bar spans 1,000 km on the ground, measured along the parallel.
claims.source: Mercator x is proportional to longitude, so the bar covers the same difference in longitude (17.99 degrees) at every latitude; along the parallel that is 2,000 x cos 60 = 1,000 km. The readout measures along the parallel (the straight east-west line on Mercator); the great-circle chord would be 996.9 km, 0.3% shorter (artifacts/scratch/w1-tissot.mjs).

claims.text: Mercator's stretch is 1 / cos(latitude): it grows toward the poles, and is 2 at 60°.
claims.source: Snyder (1987), Map Projections: A Working Manual, USGS PP 1395, ch. 7: Mercator scale factor k = h = sec(latitude). sec 60 = 2.000; sec 70 = 2.924. v2: the reveal no longer names 70° (never gated); it quotes the recorded 60°N readouts and, if the bar has moved, the learner's current Map stretch readout. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED on derivation (Snyder not opened). Own d3-geo run on the lesson projection (rotate -40, its scale): screen length per ground km, relative to the equator, both east-west and north-south, is 1.1547, 1.4142, 2.0000, 2.3662 at 30, 45, 60, 65°, equal to 1/cos(lat) to 4 decimals; it rises with latitude and is 2.00 at 60°. The stage readout stretchText(60) = "2.00×", and the Seen line records it at the 60°N milestone. · v3 (2026-10-14, demo-builder, learner r8 fit): reveal sentence now 'The stretch grows toward the poles' (was 'the farther north you go'). Previous verdict void; needs re-check. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own d3-geo run on the lesson projection (rotate −40, its scale): screen length per ground km relative to the equator, east-west and north-south, is 1.1547, 1.4142, 2.0000, 2.3662 at 30, 45, 60, 65°, equal to 1/cos(lat) to 3-4 decimals. Re-derived: y = R ln tan(π/4 + φ/2), dy/dφ = R sec φ, and the parallel's ground length is R cos φ per radian of longitude. stretchText(60) = '2.00×', recorded in the Seen line. Snyder not opened; not needed.

claims.text: Mercator's stretch is the same north-south as east-west, which is why shapes look right while sizes do not.
claims.source: Snyder (1987) ch. 7: Mercator is conformal (h = k), so small shapes are preserved while areas scale by sec^2(latitude). · v3 (2026-10-14, demo-builder, learner r8): sentence cut from the reveal ('It is the same north-south as east-west, which is why shapes look right while sizes do not'); told context, word budget (learner r8, the reviewer's named candidate). Withdrawn, not learner-visible.

claims.text: One scale bar on a world map is true along only one line.
claims.source: On Mercator the scale is true only along the equator (or two standard parallels for secant forms) (Snyder 1987 ch. 7). No flat map has constant scale everywhere (Snyder ch. 1). The lesson's statement is about this world map. · v3 (2026-10-14, demo-builder, learner r8 fit): reveal sentence now 'so one scale bar is true along only one line'. Previous verdict void; needs re-check. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. For this lesson's (tangent) Mercator map, the stretch sec φ equals 1 only at φ = 0 (own scan of −4..68°: only 0), so a fixed scale bar is true only along the equator. The reveal sentence is about this map ('The stretch grows toward the poles, so one scale bar is true along only one line'). Note: the claim text 'on a world map' read generally would be too broad (secant and equidistant projections differ); verified as scoped by its source note to this map.

claims.text: The dashed line labelled 'equator' on the map is latitude 0°, drawn by the same Mercator projection as the bar.
claims.source: Demo.tsx: eqY = projection([40, 0])[1]; line across the map at that y with the label 'equator'. v3 (2026-10-14, demo-builder): added so the reveal's 'as at the equator' points at something on the map. Needs check. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Demo.tsx: eqY = projection([40, 0])[1] (own d3-geo: y = 250.26 of 262), a full-width dashed line at that y and the text 'equator' 4 px above it, from the same projection as the bar.

recall.question: On a Mercator world map, a scale bar is drawn near the equator. You use it to measure a road in Norway, far north. Your answer will be:
recall.why: Mercator stretches the map more toward the poles, so a northern road looks longer on the map than its true length; measuring it with an equator scale bar overestimates it.
